events.title: Craft CMS 1.0 released
events.summary: [Pixel] & Tonic released Craft [CMS] 1.0 on June 4, 2013 — a flexible PHP content management system with live preview and custom fields.
events.about: Craft gave developers Matrix fields, live preview, and Twig templating without WordPress plugin sprawl — born from the ExpressionEngine add-on ecosystem. It became the preferred [CMS] for agencies building bespoke content sites before headless took over.

narrative.whyChosen: Craft [CMS] proved a modern PHP [CMS] could compete with WordPress on developer experience.
narrative.whyImportant: Matrix fields and live preview set new standards for flexible content modeling.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers wanted [CMS] power without WordPress bloat or ExpressionEngine rigidity.

events.title: Snowden NSA surveillance programs revealed
events.summary: The Guardian published the first Edward Snowden leaks on June 5, 2013 — exposing NSA bulk collection of Verizon phone records and PRISM access to major internet companies' user data.
events.about: Snowden's disclosures forced Google, Microsoft, Apple, and Facebook to publish transparency reports, encrypt traffic by default, and fight gag orders in court. Engineers accelerated [HTTPS] everywhere, end-to-end encryption in messaging apps, and zero-trust security models — while governments debated backdoors and mass surveillance reform.

narrative.whyChosen: Snowden's leaks were the catalyst for default encryption and cloud transparency reporting.
narrative.whyImportant: They made privacy engineering a mainstream product requirement, not a niche concern.
narrative.problemSolved: Users and developers lacked visibility into how governments accessed data held by tech platforms.
